title: Which expression fits each of the three problems?
description: Three small problems about lace, ribbon and flour each ask for one expression to be chosen and then simplified. The video reads each story to decide whether the total is shared among some or counted in equal pieces, then divides using the reciprocal.
teaching_notes: One idea: sharing a total among some uses the total divided by the number sharing, and counting equal pieces uses the total divided by the size of one piece. Watch for students who multiply because the numbers look small.

source: Figure it Out (problems with fractions): choose the expression that describes the solution, then simplify it, for the lace, the ribbon and the flour.
video_script.why: A learner picks the right division for each story by asking whether the total is shared or counted in pieces.
video_script.substitution: the book's own lace, ribbon and flour problems
video_script.anchor: eight metres of lace, a half metre of ribbon and five kilograms of flour
video_script.payoff_line: The three answers are thirty two bags, one sixteenth of a metre and thirty loaves.

final_answer.spoken: thirty two bags, one sixteenth of a metre and thirty loaves

video_script.fraction_reading: one quarter, one half, one sixth, one eighth, one sixteenth
video_script.design: Three rows, one for each story, each with its total, its piece and the expression it needs; the working band builds the three divisions in turn.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; three rows: a roll of lace, a strip of ribbon with eight badges, a bag of flour with loaves

marks.lace: the lace row appears with bags
marks.ribbon: the ribbon row appears with eight badges
marks.flour: the flour row appears with loaves
marks.ask: a question mark appears beside all three rows

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book with three small problems.
<bookmark mark='lace'/>A student bought eight metres of lace for school bags. Each bag used one quarter of a metre, and the lace was finished.
<bookmark mark='ribbon'/>One half of a metre of ribbon makes eight badges.
<bookmark mark='flour'/>A baker needs one sixth of a kilogram of flour for one loaf, and has five kilograms.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which expression describes each problem?

beats.on_screen: the three rows stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two small pictures: a total split into equal shares, and a total cut into equal pieces to count

marks.share: a total is split among some shares
marks.count: a total is cut into pieces that are counted
marks.both: both pictures are marked with a division sign

narration: <bookmark mark='share'/>When a total is shared equally among some, we divide the total by the number sharing.
<bookmark mark='count'/>When we count how many equal pieces fit in a total, we divide the total by one piece.
<bookmark mark='both'/>In both cases dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal.

beats.on_screen: Given: lace 8 m, 1/4 m for each bag; ribbon 1/2 m for 8 badges; flour 1/6 kg for one loaf, 5 kg in all
narration: <bookmark mark='lace'/>Given, eight metres of lace, with one quarter of a metre for each bag.
<bookmark mark='ribbon'/>One half of a metre of ribbon for eight badges.
<bookmark mark='flour'/>One sixth of a kilogram of flour for a loaf, and five kilograms in all.

beats.on_screen: To find: the right expression and its value for each problem

marks.find: the words expression and value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to choose the expression for each problem and then simplify it.

marks.eq: the line bags times one quarter equals eight is written
marks.div: eight divided by one quarter is written
marks.recip: the reciprocal four replaces one quarter

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step one, the lace. The number of bags times one quarter of a metre is eight metres.
<bookmark mark='div'/>The expression is eight divided by one quarter, the total divided by one piece.
<bookmark mark='recip'/>The reciprocal of one quarter is four, so we multiply eight by four.

marks.share: one half divided by eight is written
marks.mult: the numerators and the denominators are multiplied

narration: <bookmark mark='share'/>Step two, the ribbon. One half of a metre is shared among eight badges.
The expression is one half divided by eight.
<bookmark mark='recip'/>The reciprocal of eight is one eighth, so we multiply one half by one eighth.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>That is one times one over two times eight.

marks.eq: the line loaves times one sixth equals five is written
marks.div: five divided by one sixth is written
marks.recip: the reciprocal six replaces one sixth

narration: <bookmark mark='eq'/>Step three, the flour. The number of loaves times one sixth of a kilogram is five kilograms.
<bookmark mark='div'/>The expression is five divided by one sixth.
<bookmark mark='recip'/>The reciprocal of one sixth is six, so we multiply five by six.

beats.on_screen: check: answer × size of one piece = total, for all three rows

marks.check: each row is checked by multiplying its answer back by its piece

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, put each answer back in its question.
Multiply it by the size of one piece, and we must get the total.

marks.check: the three checks are written under them

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The three answers are thirty two bags, one sixteenth of a metre and thirty loaves.
<bookmark mark='check'/>Thirty two quarters make eight, eight sixteenths make a half, and thirty sixths make five.
